correctness.rationale: The absolutely convergent Bessel winding decomposition reconstructs each flux-dependent amplitude for n≥3; relative winding phases fix the exact all-time derivative blindness sets. At even n=2r the unique antipodal two-path amplitude provides 4 sin²(phi/2)/(r!)² (Jt)^{2r} and all closer sites are higher order. At odd n=2r+1 reflected farthest vertices produce a pair sum with coefficient 8 cos²(phi)/((r+1)!)² (Jt)^{2r+2}; its potentially odd next order cancels only AFTER summing, as now correctly stated. Exact QFI uses commuting shifts and <0|S|0>=<0|S²|0>=0. Limits fixed nonblind flux; degenerate zero-probability boundary not replaced by regular Fisher inference. Independent construction via matrix exponentials, eigendecomposition and finite differences passed 784 finite checks, not asserted as infinite proof.

value.rationale: A single position measurement is a natural experimentally constrained flux estimator. The theorem gives all-size onset exponents, exact leading constants and responsible farthest vertices, plus all-time parity-specific regular-score blind loci, and quantitatively compares its information deficit to an explicitly gauge-fixed quantum benchmark. Its operational motivation arises from recent magnetic ring sensing and chiral return-sensitivity papers. The theorem does not claim optimal practical sensing, noise robustness or gauge-independent QFI.
